units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
Mother, you won’t leave us?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: I might bring shame upon you!
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Mother!
units.name: GERALD

units.text: For a little then: and if you let me, near you always.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: To MRS. ARBUTHNOT.
Come out with us to the garden.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Later on, later on.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Exeunt HESTER and GERALD.
MRS. ARBUTHNOT goes towards door L.C. Stops at looking-glass over mantelpiece and looks into it .
Enter ALICE R.C.
A gentleman to see you, ma’am.
units.name: ALICE

units.text: Say I am not at home. Show me the card.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Takes card from salver and looks at it .
Say I will not see him.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: [LORD ILLINGWORTH enters .
MRS. ARBUTHNOT sees him in the glass and starts , but does not turn round .
Exit ALICE.] What can you have to say to me to-day, George Harford?
You can have nothing to say to me.
You must leave this house.
Rachel, Gerald knows everything about you and me now, so some arrangement must be come to that will suit us all three. I assure you, he will find in me the most charming and generous of fathers.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: My son may come in at any moment. I saved you last night. I may not be able to save you again. My son feels my dishonour strongly, terribly strongly. I beg you to go.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Sitting down .
Last night was excessively unfortunate. That silly Puritan girl making a scene merely because I wanted to kiss her. What harm is there in a kiss?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Turning round .
A kiss may ruin a human life, George Harford. I know that. I know that too well.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: We won’t discuss that at present. What is of importance to-day, as yesterday, is still our son. I am extremely fond of him, as you know, and odd though it may seem to you, I admired his conduct last night immensely. He took up the cudgels for that pretty prude with wonderful promptitude. He is just what I should have liked a son of mine to be. Except that no son of mine should ever take the side of the Puritans: that is always an error. Now, what I propose is this.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Lord Illingworth, no proposition of yours interests me.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: According to our ridiculous English laws, I can’t legitimise Gerald. But I can leave him my property. Illingworth is entailed, of course, but it is a tedious barrack of a place. He can have Ashby, which is much prettier, Harborough, which has the best shooting in the north of England, and the house in St. James Square. What more can a gentleman require in this world?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Nothing more, I am quite sure.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: As for a title, a title is really rather a nuisance in these democratic days. As George Harford I had everything I wanted. Now I have merely everything that other people want, which isn’t nearly so pleasant. Well, my proposal is this.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I told you I was not interested, and I beg you to go.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: The boy is to be with you for six months in the year, and with me for the other six. That is perfectly fair, is it not? You can have whatever allowance you like, and live where you choose. As for your past, no one knows anything about it except myself and Gerald. There is the Puritan, of course, the Puritan in white muslin, but she doesn’t count. She couldn’t tell the story without explaining that she objected to being kissed, could she? And all the women would think her a fool and the men think her a bore. And you need not be afraid that Gerald won’t be my heir. I needn’t tell you I have not the slightest intention of marrying.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You come too late. My son has no need of you. You are not necessary.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What do you mean, Rachel?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: That you are not necessary to Gerald’s career. He does not require you.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I do not understand you.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Look into the garden.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: LORD ILLINGWORTH rises and goes towards window .
You had better not let them see you: you bring unpleasant memories.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: LORD ILLINGWORTH looks out and starts .
She loves him. They love each other. We are safe from you, and we are going away.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Where?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: We will not tell you, and if you find us we will not know you. You seem surprised. What welcome would you get from the girl whose lips you tried to soil, from the boy whose life you have shamed, from the mother whose dishonour comes from you?
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: You have grown hard, Rachel.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I was too weak once. It is well for me that I have changed.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I was very young at the time. We men know life too early.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: And we women know life too late. That is the difference between men and women.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: A pause .
Rachel, I want my son. My money may be of no use to him now. I may be of no use to him, but I want my son. Bring us together, Rachel. You can do it if you choose.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Sees letter on table .
There is no room in my boy’s life for you. He is not interested in you .
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT
